title: Contravariant naturality of the normalized three-transpose Weil map
statement: Fix D,C,E,S,W,X,Y,f,cf,cy,cx with the same geometric and coefficient hypotheses as the specified chosen-duality exchange. For every supplied normalized Data d and every Weil pair omega over Y, the components transposeComponent at omega are contravariantly natural in M: for v:M to N in the opposite pair category, Hom(F(v),1) followed by the component at N equals the component at M followed by Q Hom(v,1). This only asserts the naturality square for the original three transposes; no dualizing choices, comparison substitution or final exchange is included.

source.place: Item DAG Step 6: lem-sf-tensor-hom Steps 1--2, first-variable naturality of the projection/evaluation and adjunction chain.

proof.text:
For a Weil arrow $u:M\to N$, put $A_M=R\mathcal Hom_Y(FM,\omega_Y)$ and $a_u=R\mathcal Hom_Y(Fu,1):A_N\to A_M$. The internal-Hom bifunctor and the natural tensor--Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations](i) give evaluation dinaturality
$$\operatorname{ev}_{FM}(1\otimes a_u)=\operatorname{ev}_{FN}(Fu\otimes1).$$
Naturality of the specified projection isomorphism [fix-prop-projection-formula] now gives the equality on $F(M\otimes PA_N)$
$$b_M F(1_M\otimes P a_u)=b_N F(u\otimes1_{PA_N}).$$
Apply the exceptional Hom bijection, the tensor--Hom bijection natural in its first variable, and the ordinary Hom bijection. Their naturality turns the left side into $\tau_M a_u$ and the right side into $Q(R\mathcal Hom_X(u,1_{G\omega_Y}))\tau_N$. Thus
$$\tau_M a_u=Q(R\mathcal Hom_X(u,1_{G\omega_Y}))\tau_N,$$
which is precisely contravariant naturality of $\tau$. The pair adjunctions are the restrictions of these same bijections (Steps 2, 4, 5), so the equality is an equality of Weil morphisms. This argument uses only naturality of the already cited bijections and of the specified projection map.
